summary: The habits every enterprise seller needs before any framework: research, questions, listening, control of the call.

skills.label: Account research
skills.definition: Arrive with a point of view on the account before the first question.
skills.evidence: The buyer confirms or corrects your account hypothesis.

talk_track.move: Open with what you already know, then ask why.
talk_track.strong: I read that this team moved under a new executive last quarter. What prompted that?
talk_track.weak: Before I share anything, how would you describe your top priorities this year?
talk_track.proof: Buyer confirms or corrects your hypothesis about the account

rep.buyer_line: What do you already know about how we run things here?
rep.off_move: Most teams like yours start with our core platform. Let me show you where it fits.

replies.elite: Mostly accountability. It sat across three teams and nobody owned the outcome end to end.
replies.weak: Those are in our annual report. I was hoping you would come in with a view.
replies.trap: You are fitting us to your slide before you know how we work.

curveball.speaker: CEO
curveball.line: Thirty seconds. Why are you in my calendar?
curveball.elite: Your last earnings call named operating cost as the priority. I think one workflow can move it this year.
curveball.weak: Thanks for making the time. I wanted to learn more about your goals for the year.
curveball.trap: We are the leading platform in this space and I would love to show you a demo.

skills.label: Discovery questioning
skills.definition: Ask open, layered questions that uncover how work happens today.
skills.evidence: The buyer describes their current process in their own steps.

talk_track.move: Ask how the work runs today, step by step, before you suggest anything.
talk_track.strong: Walk me through how a case gets worked today, from first touch to close.
talk_track.weak: What are the biggest challenges your team is facing right now?
talk_track.proof: Buyer describes the current process in their own steps

rep.buyer_line: We are open to ideas. Where do you want to start?
rep.off_move: Teams like yours usually stall at the handoff. Our agents remove it. Want to see how?

replies.elite: It comes in to a first-line team, they pull information from four systems, and anything unclear goes up a level. That handoff is where it stalls.
replies.weak: The usual ones. Volume, headcount, too many systems. That is true everywhere.
replies.trap: You are solving a handoff I have not described. Ask me how it works first.

curveball.speaker: COO
curveball.line: My team already told your competitor everything. Why should we repeat it?
curveball.elite: You should not. Walk me through only the step where work waits longest, and I will build from there.
curveball.weak: Every company is different, so it helps us to hear it first hand from you.
curveball.trap: No need. We have seen enough companies like yours to know where the gaps are.

skills.label: Listening and summarizing
skills.definition: Play the buyer’s words back so they know you heard the real problem.
skills.evidence: The buyer confirms your summary, or corrects it.

talk_track.move: Summarize in their words and check you got it right.
talk_track.strong: So the real cost is the hours your team spends, not the misses. Did I get that right?
talk_track.weak: Understood. Let me note that down and keep us moving through the agenda.
talk_track.proof: Buyer confirms your summary of their problem

rep.buyer_line: One thing before we go on. The bigger issue for us is the hours my team burns, not the misses.
rep.off_move: That is exactly why customers buy our platform. It gives those hours back on day one.

replies.elite: Yes, that is it. That is the part I have to defend at budget time.
replies.weak: Before you note anything, I am not sure that landed. The hours are the problem.
replies.trap: You went straight to your platform. I have not finished explaining the problem.

curveball.speaker: CFO
curveball.line: Let me be clear. I do not care about speed. I care about headcount next year.
curveball.elite: So the test is whether you can hold headcount flat as volume grows. Is that the number?
curveball.weak: Understood. Speed and headcount usually move together, so both will improve.
curveball.trap: Then you will like our case study. One customer cut forty roles in six months.

skills.label: Up-front contract
skills.definition: Agree the agenda, the time and the possible outcomes at the start.
skills.evidence: The buyer agrees to the agenda and how the call will end.

talk_track.move: Set time, agenda and outcome, and give the buyer permission to say no.
talk_track.strong: We have 20 minutes. If this is useful we agree a next step. If not, we say so. Fair?
talk_track.weak: Thanks for the time. I will give a quick overview, then leave room for questions at the end.
talk_track.proof: Buyer agrees to the agenda and outcome

rep.buyer_line: Thanks for making time. We have about twenty minutes.
rep.off_move: Great. I have prepared a tailored demo, so I will dive straight in.

replies.elite: Fair. If it is not a fit, I would rather hear it today than in three months.
replies.weak: Questions at the end usually means no time for them. I would rather spend it on our situation.
replies.trap: A demo tailored to what? We have not told you our situation yet.

curveball.speaker: CRO
curveball.line: I have a hard stop in fifteen. Go.
curveball.elite: Then one goal: decide if a second meeting is worth your time. If not, we stop there. Fair?
curveball.weak: No problem. I will move fast through the overview and save questions for the end.
curveball.trap: Understood. I will skip the intro and jump straight into the demo.

skills.label: Objection handling
skills.definition: Understand an objection before you answer it: acknowledge, clarify, respond, confirm.
skills.evidence: The buyer narrows the objection to one root cause you can address.

talk_track.move: Acknowledge, then ask a clarifying question before you answer.
talk_track.strong: That is a fair concern. When you say liability, is it the decision itself or the audit trail?
talk_track.weak: That is a fair question. Our contract has standard indemnity language that covers it.
talk_track.proof: Buyer narrows the objection to one root cause

rep.buyer_line: If the model gets a decision wrong, who carries the liability, you or us?
rep.off_move: We have never had a customer face that. Our accuracy benchmarks lead the market.

replies.elite: The audit trail. If a decision is challenged, we need to show exactly how it was made.
replies.weak: Standard language is what worries me. I need to know who owns a wrong decision, not who pays for it.
replies.trap: Every vendor tells us that. I need an answer for the day it does happen.

curveball.speaker: CISO
curveball.line: Your last release had a public security incident. Why would I trust you?
curveball.elite: That is fair to raise. Is the concern the incident itself, or how we disclosed and fixed it?
curveball.weak: That was a minor issue, fully resolved within a week. It did not affect customers.
curveball.trap: Every vendor has incidents. Ours was smaller than what your current provider had.

skills.label: Next-step control
skills.definition: End every conversation with a dated next step and a named owner.
skills.evidence: The buyer commits to a named owner and a date.

talk_track.move: Propose a specific next step with a date, owner and purpose.
talk_track.strong: Can we put 30 minutes with your security lead on the calendar for Tuesday?
talk_track.weak: I will send a recap with next steps and a few times that could work.
talk_track.proof: Buyer agrees a named owner and a date

rep.buyer_line: This was useful. What happens next?
rep.off_move: Let us loop back after you have socialized it internally.

replies.elite: Tuesday afternoon should work. I will check their calendar and confirm today.
replies.weak: A recap will sit in my inbox. Put the time on the calendar while we are here.
replies.trap: If we wait for that, this goes cold. Nobody here owns the next step yet.

curveball.speaker: VP Operations
curveball.line: Send me something and I will take a look.
curveball.elite: I will. Can we also hold twenty minutes on Thursday with your finance lead to test the numbers?
curveball.weak: Happy to. I will send the deck and a summary by end of day.
curveball.trap: Sure. I will check back in a couple of weeks to see where you landed.
